'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[Western Syria clashes (December 2024–present)|Western Syria clashes]]
***[[2025 massacres of Syrian Alawites]], [[March 2025 Western Syria clashes]]
****One war monitor says that over 1,300 [[Syrians]] are killed within 72 hours amid ongoing clashes between the [[First Syrian transitional government|transitional government]] and [[Neo-Ba'athism|pro-Assad forces]], including at least 973 [[Alawites]], [[Christianity in Syria|Christians]], and civilians of other [[Minority religion|religious minorities]] killed in [[Extrajudicial killings|reprisal massacres]] by fighters associated with the [[First Syrian transitional government|Syrian Transitional Government]]. [https://www.npr.org/2025/03/09/nx-s1-5322458/syria-revenge-killings-alawites-latakia (NPR)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx20p0pj931o (BBC News)] 
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip (2023–present)|Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip]]
***The [[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli military]] cuts off the [[electric power distribution]] supply for the [[Gaza Strip]], affecting over 2 million [[Palestinians]] and causing a [[desalination|desalination plant]] that supplies [[drinking water]] to reduce its water output. [https://apnews.com/article/gaza-israel-palestinians-war-news-ba90f0de3d4f64a1762d1a39f787817f (AP)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Military aid to Ukraine]], [[France–Ukraine relations]], [[France–Russia relations]]
***[[Ministry of Armed Forces (France)|French Armed Forces Minister]] [[Sebastien Lecornu]] says that [[France]] will use €195 million in interest from [[Russia]]n assets to fund a military aid package to [[Ukraine]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/france-tap-russian-assets-195-million-euros-this-year-minister-says-2025-03-09/ (Reuters)]
*[[War against the Islamic State]]
**[[Kivu conflict]], [[2025 Democratic Republic of the Congo attacks]]
***Nine people are killed by [[Islamic State – Central Africa Province|Islamic State]]-aligned [[Allied Democratic Forces]] rebels in [[Lubero Territory]], [[North Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://apnews.com/article/congo-islamic-state-attack-north-kivu-8f06e3de949c3f3fe15fe45f5240141e (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Reactions to the 2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses]]
**[[U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] arrests [[Mahmoud Khalil (activist)|Mahmoud Khalil]], a [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] student who played a prominent role during [[2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses|pro-Palestinian protests]] at [[Columbia University]], and revoke his [[green card]] and [[student visa]]. '''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025 Liberal Party of Canada leadership election]]
**[[Mark Carney]] wins a landslide victory in the [[Liberal Party of Canada|Liberal Party]] leadership election, with 86.85% of the vote, becoming [[prime minister–designate]] of [[Canada]], replacing [[Justin Trudeau]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/livestory/liberal-leadership-race-mark-carney-elected-in-a-landslide-9.6678061 (CBC News)]
*[[2025 Romanian presidential election]]
**Nationalist candidate [[Călin Georgescu]], the first-round winner in the [[2024 Romanian presidential election|2024 election]], is barred from running in the [[2025 Romanian presidential election|2025 election]] by the [[Permanent Electoral Authority (Romania)|Central Electoral Bureau]]. [https://www.g4media.ro/breaking-biroul-electoral-central-a-respins-candidatura-lui-calin-georgescu.html (G4 Media)]
**In [[Bucharest]], [[Romania]], protests erupt in front of the Electoral Bureau with clashes with the [[Romanian Police|police]]. [https://apnews.com/article/romania-georgescu-election-d0541a5bc20ddf7be0689d1813f9495c (AP)]
